prompt: elt_royalty_tail's 2031 row would sell 120000.00 bbl at 100.000000 USD against opex of 10000000.00, and with the limit on the ledger ends at 2030. Why was a year whose gross revenue exceeds its opex trimmed?

The test is taxable income after the loss offset, and the 2031 row would have banked a loss with no year after it to spend it.
The test is revenue less royalty against opex, and after the 20 percent royalty the year falls short of 10000000.00.

prompt: A reader runs elt_off_tail_kept without touching apply_economic_limit and reads NPV 13987603.31 and IRR null. What did the default decide?
options: To keep the 2032 row: a net cash flow of -9200000.00, a 14200000.00 loss nothing will spend, a terminal negative that costs the ledger its rate, and a KPI line reading economic_limit_year not reported.
To trim the 2032 row and report the trimmed NPV, since a year selling 10000.00 bbl against 10000000.00 of opex fails the test whether or not the flag is set.
To keep the row but exclude it from the NPV, so 13987603.31 is the value of the two producing years alone.
To test the row on taxable income rather than operating margin, which -14200000.00 fails, and to trim it on that basis.
explanation: With apply_economic_limit true the row goes and the KPIs read NPV 21590909.09, IRR 200.0000 percent, economic_limit_year 2031, rows 2.

prompt: abandonment_final_year adds a 10000000.00 lump sum to the 2031 row: net cash flow falls from 37500000.00 to 27500000.00 while tax stays 32500000.00 and taxable income 65000000.00. Why did the tax not move?
options: The engine deducted it and then added back the same 10000000.00 as depreciation recapture, so the two cancel on the tax line.
The lump sum is deductible but only against the loss pool, and the pool was empty in 2031, so the deduction waits for a year that never comes.
The cost is deducted from the following year's taxable income, and 2031 is the last modeled year, so the deduction was never reached.
The outflow is charged after the cascade has finished; the engine refuses to deduct the lump sum from any base.
explanation: Total tax on every abandonment case equals the total without abandonment, 65000000.00 on the two-year case and 148425219.46 on AKATA; NPV falls from 21590909.09 to 12500000.00, the lump sum discounted one year.

prompt: With abandonment_year 2033 on the two-year case the engine appends a row with no revenue, depreciation of 5000000.00 and a net cash flow of -10000000.00, and NPV is 14077761.08 against 12500000.00 with the cost in 2031. What is the appended row doing?

Earning two more years of price escalation, which lifts the 2033 row above the 2031 one.
Spreading the 10000000.00 across 2032 and 2033 as two half payments, so each is discounted more lightly than the whole.
Relieving the abandonment cost against the depreciation of 5000000.00, which is why NPV rises rather than falls.
explanation: The 2033 flow discounts to -7513148.01 against -10000000.00 undiscounted; the IRR is null against 120.0000 percent with the cost in 2031, because the appended row hands the vector a terminal negative.

prompt: AKATA at a 100 percent working interest with a 60000000 lump sum reports NPV 38666394.86 and a unit technical cost of 45.475732; at 50 percent the same entry reports NPV 2398979.53 and 50.944861. What should the 50 percent partner have entered?

The cost net of tax relief, since the partner's share of the deduction is what the engine expects in the abandonment column.
The share of the cost, because the lump sum is charged in full against the share flows and the engine will not scale it.
Twice the cost, so that the engine's halving returns the field-level 60000000 the partner is jointly liable for.

The contributions are charged after tax like the lump sum, but splitting the outflow across two years discounts the second half more gently, and that discounting difference alone accounts for the whole gain.

The contribution rides the opex lane, so taxable income falls to 60000000.00 and tax to 30000000.00 a year, and the final spend is paid from the fund with no further outflow.

prompt: pia_sinking_fund contributes 30000000.00 in 2025, a year under the PIA: HCT falls from 285784994.46 to 276784994.46 and CIT from 299472494.46 to 290472494.46. What happens to the TET of 31747249.45?

It falls by 3 percent of the 30000000.00, to 30847249.45, because TET is charged on the CIT assessable profit the contribution reduces.

NPV falls from 141236909.83 to 130136909.83 and the unit technical cost rises from 26.438356 to 28.082192 USD per boe. The 2.5 percent rate belongs to years before 2023.

prompt: On AKATA a fund from 2029 pays seven contributions of 8571428.57 and relieves the most tax, total 124585925.52, yet reports NPV 44902775.54 and IRR 21.9086 percent against the 2032 fund's 47415100.31 and 23.9820 percent on a total tax of 127157354.09. Why does the fund that relieves more tax score lower on both?
options: Its money leaves earlier, and an outflow moved into the early years costs more in present value and in rate than the extra relief it buys.
Its seven contributions of 8571428.57 are discounted at the real rate while its IRR is computed on the nominal flows, so the two readings use different money.
Its IRR is one root of two and the engine reported the lower one; read at the other root the early fund wins on both.
Its relief lands on the levy base, which the engine refuses to relieve, so the 124585925.52 counts tax that was never actually saved.
explanation: Starting in 2032 pays four contributions of 15000000.00 and gives the higher NPV because the money leaves later; both funds beat the lump sum's 38666394.86, which reports no rate at all because its terminal negative leaves the IRR null.

prompt: pia_sinking_fund_wi_50 runs at a 50 percent working interest and reports total fund contributions of 30000000.00 beside a total_abandonment_cost and an abandonment_cost_funded of 30000000.00, with NPV 59518454.92. What does the agreement between those three figures say?

An overfunded fund, the surplus released to the contractor in the final row, which is why the contributions exceed what the partner owes.

prompt: AKATA at a three-year shift lists rows for 2029, 2030 and 2032 onward with no 2031 row. NPV fell from 40880824.32 at two years to 17894126.42 and IRR fell from 14.6753 to 11.6363 percent, both as they should, yet payback shortened from 4.96 to 4.90 years. Which reading cannot be trusted?

The NPV, which double-discounted the empty year and fell further than the delay alone can explain.
None of them, because a ledger with a missing calendar year is refused by the engine and the KPIs printed are those of the two-year run carried forward unchanged.
The payback, which is counted on rows rather than on calendar years, so the missing row made the delay look a year shorter to it.
explanation: A longer wait for the same money cannot shorten a payback. The IRR and the NPV both fell with the delay, so only the payback, counted on rows, misreads the missing year.
